title: Transforming Text with tr & sed 🌀
description: Translate characters with tr and perform powerful search‑replace operations with sed.

slides.title: `tr` – Translate Characters 🔄
slides.content:
## A Simple Character Swapper

`tr` reads from stdin and replaces or deletes characters. It works on single characters, not strings.

- `tr 'a-z' 'A-Z'` – convert lower to uppercase.
- `tr -d ' '` – delete all spaces.
- `tr -s ' '` – squeeze repeated spaces into one.

Example: `echo "Hello World" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'`

slides.title: `sed` – Stream Editor ✨
slides.content:
## Much More Powerful

`sed` can search and replace strings, delete lines, insert text, and more. The most common use is substitution:

```bash
sed 's/old/new/' file       # replace first occurrence on each line
sed 's/old/new/g' file      # replace all occurrences (global)
```
It can work on files or from a pipe.

quizData.question: What suffix makes sed substitution replace *every* match on a line?
quizData.explanation: The `g` flag (global) replaces all occurrences, not just the first.

slides.title: More sed Tricks 🎩
slides.content:
## Beyond Substitute

- Delete lines: `sed '3d' file` (delete line 3).
- Print only specific lines: `sed -n '5,10p' file`.
- In‑place editing: `sed -i 's/old/new/g' file` (careful!).
- Use a different delimiter if your string contains slashes: `sed 's|path/to|new/path|'`.

slides.title: ⚠️ sed -i Danger
slides.content: `-i` modifies the file in place. Always test without `-i` first, or use `-i.bak` to create a backup.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: You can chain multiple sed commands with `-e` or by separating with `;`: `sed -e 's/a/A/' -e 's/b/B/'`
